title: CognitionBioChem: A structural pharmacology workbench that reports a negative result
description:
A structural pharmacology workbench for cognition-related CNS targets, built around the discipline that a displayed number must trace to a computation. Boltz-2 v2.2.1 runs locally and produced every predicted structure; chemistry is validated with RDKit; every value carries a provenance record, and fields that were never computed render as labels rather than figures. Nine studies were pre-registered under content hashes before any data was seen, under 27 registered analysis plans counting every superseded version, and their artefacts, analysis plans and prediction runs are all under content-addressed custody in the repository.

The headline result is negative, and is the reason the project exists in this form. Across a screen of 13 candidate-receptor constructs covering 12 distinct peptides — one 41-mer is screened against two different receptors, so it is counted twice in every mean and count — and a 143-fold full-MSA rerun, designed peptides did not separate from composition-matched shuffles of their own amino acids: mean native ipTM 0.629 against a mean decoy of 0.628. That hypothesis has been falsified in all eleven retained versions of the two screening studies, across candidate sets from six to thirteen constructs.

A registered positive control then measured the null itself, and narrowed how that negative may be read. Sixteen deposited X-ray peptide-receptor complexes were folded against ten uniform random permutations of each peptide: the natives beat their own permutations in aggregate by +0.0895 ipTM (Holm p = 0.0148, 13 of 16 differences positive), but only 4 of 16 beat all ten permutations of themselves against a threshold of 5 registered in advance, and the natural separation could not be shown to exceed the designed one (Welch p = 0.107). The per-candidate reading of the composition-matched null is withdrawn throughout the repository as a result: the screen's negative result is a statement about a batch of designs, and the null licenses no verdict on any single one. That control is also the only study in the slate whose protocol audit records no deviation from its registered plan; the other eight deviated in at least one respect and each says so.

An earlier version of this project displayed fabricated affinity, confidence and safety values as though they had been computed. Those claims are preserved under retracted_claims rather than deleted, and the renderers that produced them are gone. The repository ships 51 structures it computed or downloaded, the artefacts of 9 studies, 27 registered analysis plans and 12 verification suites in which every check is itself verified to fail on the defect it names.

Development note: this project was built with substantial AI assistance, and its internal review was a multi-agent LLM process rather than human peer review. Both facts are stated in the README and NOTICE.

Licensing. This deposit is not single-licensed. The project's own code is Apache-2.0, but it redistributes third-party scientific data that keeps its own terms: UniProt and AlphaFold DB under CC BY 4.0, RCSB crystal depositions under CC0 1.0, Boltz-2 model outputs under MIT, and ChEMBL-derived files under CC BY-SA 3.0 -- share-alike, so that last one carries obligations onward.
